claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential combined with free-energy perturbation can predict melting properties across high-entropy alloys.
The proposed method can replace liquid-phase EAM potentials and full thermodynamic integration.
The machine-learning potential is trained on high-fidelity electronic-structure data.
The machine-learning potential captures complex multispecies interactions in high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning potential captures local atomic rearrangements near melting.
Capturing multispecies interactions and local rearrangements improves the representation of liquid-phase behavior at melting.
Free-energy perturbation circumvents the extensive sampling required by thermodynamic integration.
Combining the machine-learning potential with free-energy perturbation enables efficient tracking of solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Tracking solid–liquid free-energy differences accurately determines melting temperature.
The method can determine enthalpy and entropy of fusion, volume change at melting, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
Predicted melting and liquid-phase properties will have errors below 5% relative to experiments and high-accuracy conventional simulations.
The proposed method will provide significant computational-efficiency gains over EAM with full thermodynamic integration.
Full thermodynamic integration can be computationally expensive.
Conventional liquid-phase EAM approaches may struggle with the compositional complexity of high-entropy alloys.
The approach is intended for compositions and temperatures represented in the machine-learning training data.
The approach may be less reliable for out-of-sample compositions or temperatures.
The approach may be less reliable when strong electronic correlations dominate.
Extremely large free-energy fluctuations near phase transitions may propagate errors in free-energy perturbation.
The simulations are to be performed near melting under NPT conditions.
